title: Black-box conversion to dominant-strategy truthfulness without expected-welfare loss
area: Algorithmic game theory, mechanism design and fair division
formal: For the finite rational single-parameter model below, is there a polynomial-query black-box transformation to dominant-strategy truthfulness in expectation that loses no expected welfare?
definitions:
There are n agents. Agent i has a finite publicly listed support V_i⊆Q_≥0 with publicly listed positive rational probabilities F_i summing to one; values are independent. All supports and probabilities have total bit length L. Reports are restricted to these supports. A deterministic oracle A accepts any profile in ∏_i V_i and returns an allocation x∈[0,1]^n∩Q^n with each coordinate encoded in at most B bits, where B is supplied. There is an arbitrary unknown feasible set X⊆[0,1]^n containing every oracle output; no downward closure, membership oracle or explicit description is supplied.

A simulator on an actual reported profile may make adaptive queries to A at other profiles and must output one allocation returned by one of its queries, with no permutation or coordinate modification unless that modified vector is itself an observed output. It also returns rational payments. It may sample from the listed priors with fresh private coins, but has no stored exponential advice or free preprocessing. All work, queried input lengths and payment output lengths have expected polynomial cost in n+L+B, on every profile, and the expected number of oracle queries is polynomial in those parameters. Oracle evaluation itself is charged one call plus reading its answer.

For every i, v_i,v_i′∈V_i and v_−i∈∏_{j≠i}V_j, require E[v_i x_i(v_i,v_−i)−p_i(v_i,v_−i)]≥E[v_i x_i(v_i′,v_−i)−p_i(v_i′,v_−i)], with expectations over simulator randomness only. Payments must be integrable; no individual-rationality or no-subsidy requirement is imposed in this variant. Require E_{v∼∏F_i,coins}[∑_i v_i x_i(v)]≥E_{v∼∏F_i}[∑_i v_i A_i(v)] exactly, without ε loss. One uniform transformation must work for every such prior and oracle.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof of the proposition or its negation for the stated model. Bayesian truthfulness, preservation only up to an additive loss, or impossibility only for MIDR transformations does not settle this stated variant.
context:
Lucier’s contributed problem distinguishes expected-welfare preservation under DSIC from stronger transformation restrictions and worst-case approximation preservation.

The earlier black-box paper gives impossibility results whose mechanism-class restrictions must be retained when comparing them with this question.
why: This asks whether algorithmic welfare can be retained when incentives are strengthened beyond Bayesian truthfulness.

import_provenance.original_title: Black-box conversion to dominant-strategy truthfulness without expected-welfare loss
import_provenance.original_statement: Can a polynomial-query black-box transformation turn any allocation algorithm for independent, known single-parameter value distributions into a truthful-in-expectation dominant-strategy mechanism preserving its expected welfare? The transformation learns feasibility only from the allocation algorithm’s outputs; the benchmark is average welfare under the prior, not a worst-case approximation guarantee.
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: Bayesian incentive-compatible reductions are known, and stronger MIDR reductions or preservation of worst-case approximation are impossible; neither answers this expected-welfare DSIC question.

sentences: Independent finite type distributions are explicitly known.
The original allocation algorithm is accessible only through oracle calls.
Feasibility can be certified only for allocations actually returned by the oracle.
The transformed mechanism must be truthful for each fixed vector of other reports.
Expected welfare must match or exceed the original algorithm with no additive loss.
